title: Owner access and scenario isolation
narration: The real process per request adapter initializes a scenario, allows its owner to read and denies access after revocation. A second trusted setup replaces scenario tables in one transaction. Invalid replacement rolls back. Production initialization remains separate and refuses to overwrite an authority. Expected policy errors return structured JSON without pretending the process crashed.

title: Real protected reads
narration: Protected reads use real M L KEM seven sixty eight encapsulation. The proof is the exact organizer specified HMAC over the challenge concatenated with stored content. An independent Python implementation generated sixteen keys, decapsulated the actual Linux adapter responses and recomputed the proofs. Signature verification also passes two hundred twenty five pinned independent vectors.

title: Signed rotation and recovery
narration: Network commands bind the authority, actor, key fingerprint, epoch, nonce, expiry and operation. Rotation verifies possession of the replacement key and commits the cutoff atomically. In flight transfers continue only during the old key's valid grace period. Two distinct custodians approve loss recovery, and stale approvers or competing proposals fail.

title: Independent nodes, bounded stale access
narration: Each read node has its own encrypted cache and verified policy chain. Its lease starts when it sends a fresh challenge, so delaying a response cannot renew stale access. Three nodes receive delayed updates; two are partitioned and expire closed. These are five observed samples. The mathematical authorization bound requires a progressing monotonic clock; it is not a physical network latency guarantee.

title: Crash safety and audit availability
narration: The suite actually kills a process during an uncommitted rotation and checks recovery. Authentication, effects and signed audit records share a transaction. Forged requests now update bounded minute counters instead of filling the signed log. Reaching the normal audit budget cannot block revocation or recovery. Physical disk failure remains a real limit to durable commits.

title: Backups and signed history
narration: File contents and identity backups are encrypted. Signed SHA three eighty four audit chains preserve record boundaries and correlation history. A trusted checkpoint detects an older restored backup. Status checks new links after its verified prefix; full exported history can be checked independently. Master keys are beside the database, so encryption protects database only leaks, not an entire compromised host.

title: Encrypted client delivery
narration: The recipient signs a one use ephemeral key offer bound to both peers. The sender encapsulates, derives a transcript bound key and encrypts locally. The relay stores ciphertext. Reordered and duplicate chunks are handled, conflicting or modified chunks fail, and incomplete messages expire. Real CLI processes transfer a file and acknowledge it. Session resumption is deliberately unsupported.

title: Detection beyond the practice set
narration: The main detector result uses four thousand reference observations and twelve thousand later held out events. Service, role and action names change with the seed. Role state, independent approval, revocation and time decayed connected paths drive the rules. Labels are used only for scoring. F one is about point nine four, including one hundred twenty measured misses.

title: Input diversity and realistic limits
narration: Timestamp offsets and fractional seconds are normalized while raw evidence remains. Missing optional correlation fields do not crash ingestion. Paths can span seventy second gaps and different flow IDs. Legitimate re grants are distinguished from later revocation. Benign novel paths are not automatically attacks. The reported eighty three second median delay includes deliberately late collection, not just computation time.
